name: Honda CB550 Four
engine: 544 cc air-cooled SOHC inline four, four carbs
intro: The middle of Honda's SOHC four family, between the CB500 and CB750. Tough engine; neglect is its main enemy.
focus: Rebuild and sync as a set
Check inside and at the pivot

A-003.title: Get the service manual
A-003.instructions: Get the Honda factory service manual for your year, or the Haynes manual that covers the CB400F and CB550 fours.
A-003.reason: Every torque value, clearance and capacity in this course comes from the manual.

G-004.title: Rebuild the four carbs as a set
G-004.instructions: Take the carb bank off as one unit. Strip one carb at a time and keep each one's parts in its own tray. Clean every jet and passage, fit new gaskets and o-rings, set the float heights, refit, then sync all four.
G-004.reason: Dried gaskets, varnished jets and stuck float needles are the usual trouble after storage.

add.title: Listen for cam chain noise
add.instructions: Start it cold and listen at the top of the engine. A rattle that won't settle points at a stretched cam chain or tired tensioner.
add.reason: A stretched cam chain is common on high-mileage engines and can damage the top end if left.

add.title: Check the frame at the swingarm pivot
add.instructions: Clean and inspect the lower frame rails and the area around the swingarm pivot for rust.
add.reason: That's where frame rust usually starts on these bikes.

G: Look inside the tank with a light. Internal rust needs a liner kit or a new tank before it clogs the rebuilt carbs.

recallNote: Any recalls on bikes this old were closed long ago.

known.title: Gummed carbs
known.what: Dried gaskets, varnished jets and stuck floats after storage.
